prompt:
You are a sceptical financial analyst reviewing a forecast prepared by a colleague.

Given the following forecast for SBIN (base year 2022):
{
  "strategy": "alt_strategy",
  "base_year": 2022,
  "anomaly_detected": true,
  "forecast": [
    {
      "year": 2023,
      "revenue_cr": 441000,
      "net_income_cr": 42000,
      "eps": 47.1
    },
    {
      "year": 2024,
      "revenue_cr": 481000,
      "net_income_cr": 50000,
      "eps": 56.07
    },
    {
      "year": 2025,
      "revenue_cr": 524000,
      "net_income_cr": 59000,
      "eps": 66.19
    }
  ],
  "top_assumptions": [
    "Total Income (Interest Earned + Other Income) on consolidated basis grows at ~9-10% per annum, blending the FY2022 YoY growth of ~6% (consolidated total income rose from ~385,338 cr in FY2021 to ~406,973 cr in FY2022) with the underlying credit-cycle recovery trajectory and management's guidance of double-digit advance growth continuing into FY2023; the anomaly flag is set because FY2022 Net Profit surged ~58% YoY (from ~22,405 cr to ~35,374 cr consolidated) largely due to sharp NPA provisioning reduction and an exceptional employee-pension charge in operating expenses, making the profit jump non-recurring in its pace, hence PAT growth is moderated to ~18-20% for FY2023 before normalising to ~15% thereafter.",
    "Net Interest Margin stabilises or marginally improves as RBI's rate-hike cycle (repo +40 bps off-cycle announced near March 2022 end) passes through to loan yields faster than deposit repricing, supporting interest income growth; NPA trajectory continues improving (Gross NPA fell from 4.98% to 3.97% standalone) reducing incremental provisioning needs and sustaining PAT expansion, while macro risks (Russia-Ukraine, commodity inflation, CAD widening to >2.5% GDP) cap upside on credit growth and fee income."
  ],
  "reasoning": "This is State Bank of India (SBI Group), a bank/NBFC, so Total Income (Interest Earned + Other Income) is used as Revenues per the BANKS/NBFCs rule. Consolidated Total Income for FY2022 was approximately 406,973 cr (Revenue before exceptional items per geographic segment disclosure) versus 383,971 cr in FY2021, a YoY growth of ~6%. However, consolidated Net Profit jumped ~58% YoY to 35,374 cr from 22,405 cr, driven by a large decline in credit costs (NPA provisions normalising post-COVID) and a one-time exceptional pension charge partially offsetting \u2014 making FY2022 profit growth anomalous and not a reliable forward projection rate. The 3-year CAGR on revenue is estimated at ~7-9% given the COVID-impacted FY2020-21 base, and management guidance explicitly targets double-digit advance growth and expects India GDP growth of 7.2% in FY2023. Accordingly, revenue is projected at ~9-10% CAGR for FY2023-25, and PAT growth is moderated from the FY2022 spike to ~18-20% in FY2023 normalising to ~15% thereafter, with EPS computed on ~891 crore shares outstanding (face value Re.1 each, approximately 892.46 crore shares per Schedule 1)."
}

Step 1: Identify the 3 most critical assumptions embedded in this forecast.
Step 2: For each assumption, describe one plausible scenario where it fails.
Step 3: Rate each assumption failure as Low / Medium / High risk to the forecast accuracy.
Step 4: Assign an overall confidence score from 0-100 (100 = completely certain).

RESPONSE FORMAT: Begin your response DIRECTLY with the opening brace { — no reasoning or text before the JSON.

Return ONLY valid JSON:
{
  "company": "<COMPANY>",
  "base_year": <YYYY>,
  "strategy": "<baseline|alt_strategy>",
  "assumptions": [
    {"assumption": "<text>", "failure_scenario": "<text>", "risk": "<Low|Medium|High>"}
  ],
  "confidence_score": <0-100>,
  "overall_critique": "<2 sentences>"
}
